description: We are a passionate team of students and a dedicated teacher from Dunia Alajial International School, united by our love for space, science, technology, and innovation. Combining skills in AI, software development, research, design, and problem-solving, we aim to turn NASA data into creative solutions for real-world challenges. We are excited to collaborate, learn, and build something impactful at NASA Space Apps!

🌱 **AgriPulse – From Space to Soil**

AgriPulse is an interactive agricultural decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

By integrating NASA Earth observation data with weather information and farmer-provided field records, AgriPulse helps farmers better understand their land, explore crop rotation strategies, and make more informed agricultural decisions.

The platform combines NASA POWER climate data, satellite imagery layers, soil observations, water availability, crop planning, and transparent financial scenarios in one accessible workspace.

With simple and advanced modes, interactive maps, and downloadable reports, AgriPulse makes complex environmental information easier to understand and use.

**Our mission is to bridge the gap between space technology and sustainable agriculture, empowering farmers to turn Earth observation data into practical insights.**

🔗 Explore our open-source project on GitHub: https://github.com/ameer-marwan/AgriPulse
details:
🌱 AgriPulse – From Space to Soil

Transforming NASA Earth Observation Data into Smarter Farming Decisions

🌍 1. The Problem

Farmers worldwide face increasing challenges related to water scarcity, unpredictable weather conditions, soil management, and agricultural profitability.

Although NASA provides valuable Earth observation and climate data, transforming this information into practical agricultural insights often requires technical expertise.

Our challenge is to bridge the gap between complex scientific data and everyday farming decisions.

🚀 2. Our Solution

AgriPulse is an interactive, web-based agricultural decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our platform brings together NASA Earth observation resources, regional climate information, farmer-provided soil records, crop planning, and financial analysis in one accessible workspace.

AgriPulse aims to help farmers understand their agricultural conditions, explore alternative crop rotation strategies, and make better-informed decisions about land and resource management.

🛰️ 3. How AgriPulse Works

Step 1 – Select Your Field 📍

Farmers can search for a location, enter coordinates, use GPS, or interact with the map to select their agricultural land.

Step 2 – Explore NASA Earth Data 🌍

AgriPulse integrates NASA POWER historical climate records and NASA GIBS satellite imagery layers to provide regional environmental context.

Available imagery includes MODIS vegetation indicators, GPM/IMERG rainfall visualization, SMAP soil-moisture layers, and SRTM terrain information.

Step 3 – Understand Weather and Soil 🌦️

The platform combines historical NASA climate information with current modeled weather forecasts from Open-Meteo.

Farmers can also enter their own soil observations, including pH, texture, drainage, and sample information.

Step 4 – Explore Crop Rotation Strategies 🌾

AgriPulse provides three exploratory crop rotation pathways focused on soil diversity, water awareness, and crop diversification.

These pathways consider the current crop, crop families, farmer priorities, water access, and available historical climate context.

They are intended to support comparison and discussion rather than provide validated field-specific planting recommendations.

Step 5 – Analyze Farm Economics 📊

Farmers can enter expected yields, selling prices, production costs, and transportation expenses to explore financial scenarios and estimated profit margins.

Step 6 – Generate Reports 📄

AgriPulse organizes the available information into downloadable reports, helping farmers review their observations, assumptions, and planning options.

💡 4. What Makes AgriPulse Innovative?

AgriPulse focuses on making Earth observation information accessible to farmers without requiring advanced scientific or programming knowledge.

Our main innovations include:

  • NASA Data Accessibility: Bringing scientific climate records and satellite imagery into a farmer-friendly workspace.
  • Two Experience Modes: Simple Farmer Mode for beginners and Advanced Mode for users who need additional planning tools.
  • Transparent Decision Support: Clearly distinguishing real data, modeled forecasts, farmer-entered information, and planning assumptions.
  • Crop Rotation Exploration: Allowing farmers to compare alternative crop-family pathways while highlighting missing evidence and limitations.
  • Integrated Farm Planning: Combining environmental context, agricultural records, and financial scenarios in one platform.
  • Global Accessibility: A browser-based solution that can support agricultural planning across different geographical regions.

💻 5. Technologies and Data Sources

AgriPulse was developed using modern web technologies and publicly available Earth observation resources.

Development Technologies:

  • HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript
  • Node.js development and build tools
  • MapLibre GL JS for interactive geographic visualization
  • Vercel for web deployment
  • GitHub for source code management and collaboration

NASA Data Resources:

  • NASA POWER – Historical temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind, and solar data
  • NASA GIBS – Earth observation imagery and map visualization
  • MODIS – Vegetation-index imagery
  • GPM / IMERG – Satellite precipitation imagery
  • SMAP – Modeled surface soil-moisture imagery
  • SRTM – Terrain and elevation visualization

Additional Data:

  • Open-Meteo – Current modeled weather forecasts and geocoding services
  • Farmer-provided soil observations, crop information, and economic assumptions

🌱 6. Expected Impact

AgriPulse aims to empower farmers, particularly those in water-scarce regions such as Saudi Arabia, by making environmental information easier to access and interpret.

The platform supports awareness of rainfall patterns, soil conditions, crop diversification, and agricultural costs.

By connecting accessible Earth observation data with practical farm planning tools, AgriPulse seeks to promote informed decision-making and more sustainable agricultural practices.

Future development will focus on validating crop suitability, incorporating field-level measurements, and improving irrigation decision support.

🔬 7. Scientific Transparency

AgriPulse distinguishes between historical NASA records, satellite imagery, modeled weather forecasts, and farmer-entered observations.

NASA GIBS layers are currently used for visual exploration and are not treated as field-level measurements or direct inputs into crop suitability calculations.

Crop rotation pathways are exploratory and require further validation using local agricultural evidence.

Financial results are scenario estimates based on user-provided assumptions.

We believe responsible innovation requires transparency about both the capabilities and limitations of technology.

🌍 Our Vision

“From Space to Soil — Making Earth Observation Data Accessible, Understandable, and Useful for Every Farmer.”
